✓
Legal first & last are separate fields. Name must match your payment method. Name & birthday lock once your email is verified; your number stays changeable — but only by verifying that email, which is how you get back in if you lose your phone.

Verify your email — enter the 6-digit code sent to your email. (Demo: any 6 digits.)

✓
This finalizes your canonical Gopher account. Your verified profile & personal info carry across Gopher Request, Connect, Go & Deals — you won't re-enter it on other platforms.

Your mobile number is how you sign in — so if you’ve lost it, we verify you by the email on your account instead.

!
Use the email already on your account. If you never verified it, you can do that here — it’s the same step you skipped at signup. (Demo: jamie@email.com is verified; jamie.unverified@email.com never was.)

We don’t recognise that address on this account.

!
That address isn’t on this account. We only ever send a recovery code to the email already on file — never to one typed in here, because that would let anyone claim an account. Check the address, or use the one you signed up with.

This address is on your account — but it was never verified, so we can’t use it to prove it’s you yet.

✓
You can do that right now. It’s the same step you skipped when you signed up: we email a 6-digit code, you enter it, and your email is verified for good.

Enter the 6-digit code we emailed to your email. (Demo: any 6 digits.)

One more check before we move your account to a new number.

✓
Your name and date of birth were locked when your email was verified, so they are what we check against here.

Enter the number you want on this account from now on.

!
We’ll text this number to prove it’s yours. Your old number stops working for sign-in the moment this is done.

Enter the 6-digit code we texted to your new number. (Demo: any 6 digits.)

Your mobile number is now your new number. Sign in with it from here on.

✓
We told both sides. A notice went to your email and to your old number — so if this wasn’t you, you’d know.
